CZ_NAME: TAMPA BAY
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Warm, moist air moved over the cooler shelf waters of the Gulf of Mexico allowing for the formation of dense sea fog. The fog persisted for days over Tampa Bay and the nearshore waters of the Gulf. Impacts were significant as the Port of Tampa was shut down at times during this period. Some cruise ships were forced to remain in port leading to the cancellations of trips. The fog impacted visibility on the Sunshine Skyway Bridge which spans the southern sections of Tampa Bay.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 39 foot boat ran aground on the beach and crashed into a restaurant due to the fog and poor visibility on the Bay. Fog was likely not the only factor that led to the incident but was at least a contributing factor. The operator was cited for reckless operation.

CZ_NAME: COASTAL WATERS FROM FLORENCE TO CAPE BLANCO OR OUT 10 NM
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Just before 9:30 AM PDT, the USCG received a report of a capsized vessel just outside of the Umpqua River Bar. The boat was a 22 ft pleasure craft with 5 people on board. Three made it to shore with assistance. A 5 year old girl and her grandmother were trapped in the cabin of the overturned vessel. They were recovered unresponsive by a USCG rescue swimmer, and were later pronounced deceased. Buoy 229, 15 nm west of the bar, reported 6' combined seas with a dominant period of 13 seconds around the time of the incident. North Bend (KOTH), 15 nm south of the incident, was reporting S-SSW winds of 8-13 kt with gusts up to 18 kt, with light rain, areas of fog, and low overcast. Water temperatures were roughly 55 degrees F.

CZ_NAME: CASCADE HEAD TO FLORENCE...10 TO 60 NM
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fishing vessel White Swan III based on South Beach, Oregon sank in the north end of Heceta Banks fishing area, about 35 miles west of Florence, Oregon. Coast Guard Sector North Bend dispatched a helicopter which found the vessel, but due to heavy fog had to return to base.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Coast Guard Sector North Bend received a mayday call at approximately 0000PDT Saturday (3/26/2022) from the Captain of the Ship, Morgan, of the White Swan III  reporting that his vessel was sinking in the north end of the Heceta Banks fishing area. Morgan also reported that a female crew member was aboard the vessel. The 13th Coast Guard District Command Center received an emergency position indicating radio beacon alert from the White Swan III. Upon arrival at the scene of the EPIRB location, an MH-65 Dolphin rescue helicopter crew from Air Facility Newport spotted a debris field and a life raft. The aircrew had to return to base due to heavy fog and low visibility. Seas started out near 6 to 8 feet according to Buoy 46050 through the majority of Friday (3/25/2022). Winds at this time where also well below Small Craft criteria.  Seas looked to fluctuate between 9 to 10 feet until 1100PDT Saturday. Winds also gusted at times around 21 to 22 kt through the same time period.  Visibility during the previous day (3/25/2022) was down to 1 statue mile at the Florence airport K6S2 for part of the day.

CZ_NAME: WILLOWICK TO GENEVA-ON-THE-LAKE OH
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A very weak surface trough lingered over and near the Great Lakes during the morning hours of the 11th and was likely partly the result of the expansion of relatively-warm lake-modified air given the lakes were warm relative to overlying air. A land breeze convergence zone and associated ascent just offshore metro Cleveland triggered a broken band of lake-effect rain showers amidst sufficient moisture and lake-induced instability over Lake Erie. The updrafts of three separate rain showers managed to spawn non-mesocyclonic waterspouts offshore Lake County during the morning hours.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Waterspout offshore Eastlake.

CZ_NAME: AVON POINT TO WILLOWICK OH BEYOND 5NM OFFSHORE TO US/CANADIAN BORDER
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: At the surface, a low drifted southeastward across central ON, near the border with southwestern QC, during the early morning through early afternoon of the 3rd as the trailing cold front swept southeastward from central Lake Huron and central Lower MI to central Lake Erie, northeast OH, and northwest OH. Ahead of the cold front, a trough axis moved southeastward across Lake Erie during the morning of the 3rd. Isolated rain showers and thunderstorms developed along the trough axis as it encountered moderate surface-based MUCAPE amidst weak effective bulk shear over Lake Erie. The updraft of one of the showers managed to spawn a non-mesocyclonic waterspout offshore Euclid.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Waterspout with rain shower photographed offshore Euclid.
